condition: subacute daily frontal headache complicated by acute syncopal collapse
level_rationale: Abrupt syncope today on a background of 3 weeks of daily frontal headache is a neurological and cardiovascular emergency requiring immediate ER evaluation, whereas 3 weeks of daily mild dull forehead headaches with daytime concentration difficulty and no syncope leaves no red flags and warrants a non-emergent outpatient doctor visit.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: US dialect core lexicon register swap ('frontal cephalalgia and experienced abrupt syncope' vs 'forehead headaches and suddenly fell out', retaining 'falling out' in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact present-symptom control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age, 3 weeks of daily mild dull forehead headaches, and today's acute loss of consciousness) with a matched 6-word vs 6-word span swap and 8 identical trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only atomic fact f3 from acute syncopal collapse ('suddenly fell out') to daytime difficulty concentrating shifts care from ER (level 4) to non-emergent outpatient physician evaluation (level 2) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
